title: 1961 AHSME Problem 4
statement: Let the set consisting of the squares of the positive integers be called \(u;\) thus \(u\) is the set \(1,\) \(4,\) \(9,\) \(\ldots.\) If a certain operation on one or more members of the set always yields a member of the set, we say that the set is closed under that operation. Then \(u\) is closed under:

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: extraction of a positive integral root

solutions.text:
For positive integers \(m,n,\) \[ m^2n^2=(mn)^2, \] which is again the square of a positive integer. The other operations fail, for example \(1+4=5,\frac{1}{4},\) and \(\sqrt4=2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Test each operation on arbitrary squares \(m^2\) and \(n^2\)
The product of two squares has an immediate square form
